messages.author: 333f3e76f253995a
messages.subject: Scaling issue in 3D models
parts:
Dear list, I’m conducting a 3D GM on small mandibles with geomorph. I’m not used to work in 3D so my knowledge about meshes and 3D models is limited. All models are from microCT scanning except two, that are from a laser scanner. One problem that I’m facing is that despite the landmarks coordinates are multiplied by the scale factor, the two model from the laser scanner have an extremely low centroid size, compared with the rest of the sample. Moreover, this "size" difference do not really exists since this two specimens with a very small centroid sizes, have an average real size. The 3d landmarks are acquired with IDAV Landmark editor, saved in nts format. The scaling procedure is carried out in R,  following a modified code from geomorph 3 quick guide:

vec_scale # Vector of real distance in mm between landmarks 4 and 5 for each specimen
for (i in 1:dim(coords)[3]){
scb <- coords[4:5,,i]
scale <- sqrt((scb[1,1]-scb[2,1])^2+(scb[1,2]-scb[2,2])^2+(scb[1,3]-scb[2,3])^2)/vec_scale[i]
coords[,,i] <- coords[,,i]*scale }
coords <- coords[-(4:5),,] # remove the landmarks 4 and 5

The reason way I’m scaling in R and not in Landmark editor is that Landmark editor always save my coordinates without calibration, no matter if I check “Use calibrated coordinates based on...” when exporting the landmark coordinates.
I really don't know if I missing something in the scaling procedure or the issue is the difference in the source resolution of the models. Any tips will be very appreciated!.

Kind regards,

Ale

messages.author: 333f3e76f253995a
messages.subject: Re: Scaling issue in 3D models
parts:
Ok, the problem was in the original scale of the models, unifying the units between microct and laser models resolved the problem.
Regards,
A.
